subject: sociology
title: Methods & Methodology: Quantitative & Qualitative
welcome_lead: Numbers or narratives? Both, often together.
meta_desc: A-Level Sociology methods quantitative qualitative reliability validity.
final_note: Match method to question, not theory to dogma.

concepts.def: Used by researcher but collected by others.
Same method yields same results — repeatability.

walkthroughs.body_html: Surveys (questionnaires, structured interviews) measure attitudes at scale. Official statistics (Census, CSEW, ONS) are cheap and large. Easy to analyse statistically. Strong on reliability and representativeness; weak on validity (forced choices may miss meaning).

Unstructured interviews, focus groups, participant observation, ethnography. Rich, contextual, high validity. Subject to interviewer effect, hard to generalise. Verstehen (Weber) — empathetic understanding — central to interpretivist tradition.

Denzin (1970): triangulation uses multiple methods to cross-check. Glaser & Strauss (1967) Grounded Theory: building theory from data. Mixed methods are increasingly standard. Reflexivity requires researchers to acknowledge their own influence.
